info.title: LumenBox client API
info.description:
LumenBox client API, v1 (docs/106 §4). Additions only inside v1: a new operation, a new optional field, a new known value — each raises the revision `GET /api/v1/meta` reports.

Conventions, the same for every operation:
- JSON, camelCase. Ids are opaque strings: compare them, never parse them. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second (`2026-11-28T10:00:00Z`).
- A field with no value is absent, never null.
- A client ignores fields it does not know.
- A string listed with `x-extensible-enum` is an open enumeration: a client treats a value it does not know as "other", shows the item's plain words, and offers to open it on the page or the desktop app when it cannot act on it.
- Lists take `?limit=` (1–100) and `?cursor=` and answer `{ items, nextCursor }`; `nextCursor` is absent on the last page.
- Errors are `{ code, error, requestId }`: `code` is stable and is what a program reads; `error` is a sentence in the request's language (`Accept-Language`). Every answer carries `X-Request-Id`.
- An unknown path answers 404 `api-operation-unknown`; a known path with a method it does not take, 405 `api-method-not-allowed`. A resource the caller may not see answers 404 exactly as one that does not exist.
- Reads carry `ETag`; a request with a matching `If-None-Match` answers 304 with no body.
- Every `POST` accepts `Idempotency-Key`: a repeat within 24 hours with the same body answers the first answer —
  within 30 seconds, from memory only, for an operation whose answer or request holds a secret (`x-secret-answer`: a token, or a secret for the vault).
- 429 carries `Retry-After` in seconds.
- A deprecated operation answers with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers for a full release line before it goes. Operations listed in `meta.preview` may change in any release.

Credentials (`Authorization: Bearer`): a personal token (`lbxp_…`) is a person's own script; a service token (`lbxs_…`) is an integration an Admin named, limited to its view;
a device credential (`lbxd_…`, fifteen minutes, renewed with its refresh token `lbxr_…` at `POST /auth/refresh`) is a person's phone or desktop client.
A request body is JSON: a field the operation does not take is refused (`api-param-unknown`), and `null` is the same as absent.
What a call may do is the person's role, intersected with the token's scopes, intersected with what that person may see; a token never raises anything.
Cross-origin browser calls are not answered with CORS headers.

get.summary: What changed since a position, durably
get.description:
For a client waking from sleep, starting, or reconnecting: what changed since `since`, read from a ledger on the server's disk that survives restarts and is kept 30 days. A change is listed only when the caller may read the thing now (or, gone, could have read it); its words are fetched, not sent. Changes are of work, agents, the inbox, conversations and messages; an agent's `status` (working or idle) is not a change. Any credential: each change is shown by the scope its type needs — `work:read` for work, `agents:read` for agents, `work:decide` for the inbox, `chat:read` for conversations and messages (and a service token's view with conversation text) — and a credential without it is not told of it.

Any credential.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The `durableSeq` from the last answer; 0 the first time.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many changes at most. 1 to 1000; 500 when absent.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: An `ETag` this client holds: 304 when it still matches.

200.description: What changed since `since`, oldest first, each thing once (its newest change). When `reset` is true the gap is older than what the server keeps (30 days), or `since` is from another installation's history: drop what is cached, read it again (`/work`, `/agents`, `/board`, `/inbox` with `work:decide`, `/conversations` with `chat:read`), then go on from `durableSeq`.

get.description:
`text/event-stream`, for a client in the foreground. Each `change` event's data is a `ChangeRecord` and its `id` is the record's `seq`. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (what `EventSource` sends) and the stream first replays, from the same durable ledger as `/changes`, each thing changed since, once; then a `ready` event whose `id` is the newest position. When the gap is older than the ledger keeps, the first event is `reset` (data `{ "durableSeq": n }`): reload, then go on. With no `Last-Event-ID` the stream starts now. A `: ping` comment comes every 20 seconds. The stream ends when the credential stops being valid. What a credential may be told of is as for `/changes`.

Any credential.

post.summary: Start a device's sign-in through a channel (PKCE)
post.description:
OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE `S256` (RFC 7636), with this server as the authorization server: open `authorizationUrl` in the system's authentication browser (`ASWebAuthenticationSession`, Custom Tabs). The person signs in at the vendor and comes back to this server, which sends the browser to `redirectUri` with `code` (one use, one minute) and `state` — or with `error=access_denied` and `error_description` (`not-a-member`, `not-linked`, `vendor-refused`) when the vendor's answer lets nobody in. Then `POST /auth/oauth/exchange`.

No credential needed.

post.description:
The code and the PKCE verifier for a device credential. An activated person is `authenticated`: the answer has the device's tokens and `me`, and their own computer is made now if they are owed one and have none. A person the organisation has not let in yet is `asked_to_join`: their request waits for an Admin and no credential is issued. A code that does not work counts as a sign-in try.

No credential needed.

post.summary: Sign a device in with a pairing code a signed-in page shows
post.description:
A signed-in page (Settings → Mine → Phones) shows a QR code: `lumenbox://pair#server=<origin>&code=<code>`. The code works once, for two minutes, and is shown only after a sign-in in the last ten minutes. It signs the device in as the person who showed it. bearer.description:
A personal token (`lbxp_…`), a service token (`lbxs_…`) or a device's access token (`lbxd_…`). Scopes:
- `agents:read`: Read the agents the person may reach.
- `work:read`: Read work, its history and the board.
- `work:decide`: Answer what waits on the person: count work as done, put it off, stop it, approve or deny.
- `chat:read`: Read conversations the person may read.
- `chat:write`: Send messages and card actions in conversations the person may drive.
- `files:read`: Read deliverables.
- `devices:manage`: List and remove the person's own devices.
- `desktop:view`: Watch an agent's desktop.
- `desktop:control`: Drive an agent's desktop.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; absent on the last page.

StepUpProof.description:
A device's step-up proof (docs/110 §4): its registered key's ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 signature over `lumenbox-step-up/1
<deviceId>
<item id>
<decision>
<detail>`.

signature.description: The signature, DER or raw r||s, base64url.

ApprovalDecision.description: An answer to an approval. `decision` `allow:once`/`allow:session` in the signed text; `detail` is `-`.

scope.description: For `allow`: `once` (this call) or `session` (this agent's turn). `always` is refused here.

reason.description: For `deny`: what the agent is told.

InboxAnswer.description: An answer to a question, an Outbox draft or a secret request; nothing else is answered here. A question takes `answer` (`text`); a draft `approve`, `edit` (`body`) or `reject` (`reason`); a secret `save` (`value`) or `dismiss`. Approving signs `approve` with detail `-`; editing signs `edit` with the detail BASE64URL(SHA-256(UTF-8 `body`)), no padding; saving a secret signs `save` with the same digest of `value`. Rejecting, dismissing and answering a question need no proof.

action.description: One of the item's `actions` this operation takes: `answer`, `approve`, `edit`, `reject`, `save`, `dismiss`.

text.description: For `answer`: the words, or one of the question's `options`.

body.description: For `edit`: the words to send instead.

reason.description: For `reject`: what the agent is told.

value.description: For `save`: the secret. It goes to the vault and nowhere else — not a transcript, not a log, not a retry's memory.

WorkDecision.description: A decision on work the person asked for.

decision.description: `done`: count it as done. `keep-open`: refuse a proposal to close it. `put-off`: ask again at `until`. `stop`: stop it and drop it.

Notification.description: What a wake-only push is about (docs/110 §5): the push carried only `seq`; the words come from here, to a device that may read them.

seq.description: The position in the change record the push named.

title.description: A line for the notification's title.

Conversation.description: A conversation with an agent the caller may reach, as the page's chat lists it. A service token reads none unless its view includes conversation text.

kind.description: `main`: the agent's own, the page's chat. `chat`: an outside chat's (DingTalk, Feishu). `other`: another thread.

title.description: Its first line, or the agent's name for `main`.

updatedAt.description: When something was last written in it.

running.description: Whether the agent is in a turn in it now.

canWrite.description: Whether the caller may send in it: a driver's credential with `chat:write`.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; absent on the last page.

Message.description: One entry of a conversation, as the page draws it: never a prompt, a tool's input or a host note's words. The payload of `kind` is in the field of that name where it has one (`card`, `question`, `steps`). A kind a client does not know is shown by `text` when there is one, else skipped.

id.description: The message. Opaque; ids rise in the order of the conversation.

kind.description: `person`: what a person said. `agent`: what the agent said. `teammate`: another agent's message. `notice`: a turn nobody typed (a timer, a webhook, a restart), by `label` only. `status`: how a turn ended. `card`: a card the agent drew. `question`: a question it asked. `steps`: what it did, in words.

at.description: When it was written, when the record kept the time.

from.description: Who it is from: a teammate's name, or the chat a person wrote in (`dingtalk`, `feishu`, `telegram`, `routine`).

aside.description: An agent's words beside its steps: commentary rather than its answer.

label.description: For a `notice`: what started the turn.

files.description: Files the agent sent with these words.

sentIds.description: For `person`: the `messageId`s of what was sent and is answered here (`POST …/messages` answers one).

items.description: A step, in the request's language.

steps.description: For `steps`: what the agent did, one line each.

MessageCard.description: A card the agent drew (ShowUI). A later card with the same `surfaceId` replaces it. A client that does not draw A2UI shows `title` and opens the page.

a2ui.description: The card as A2UI v0.9 messages, a JSON array in a string, as the page draws it.

closed.description: The agent took the card away.

MessageQuestion.description: A question the agent asked: answered with a message, or at `POST /inbox/{id}/answer` while it waits.

fallback.description: What it does with no answer.

MessagePage.description: Messages, oldest first. Without `after`, the newest ones, and `nextCursor` goes back to older ones; with `after`, those after it, and `nextCursor` goes on.

nextCursor.description: The next page's cursor; absent on the last page.

SendMessage.description: A person's message to the agent. Sent twice with one `clientMessageId` (or one `Idempotency-Key`) within 24 hours, it reaches the agent once.

clientMessageId.description: The client's own id for this message, kept across retries: a UUID.

attachmentIds.description: Files uploaded to this conversation to send with it (`POST /uploads`), at most 10.

CardAction.description: A press on a card the agent drew (ShowUI): it reaches the agent as the page's press does, and continues the work the card was drawn for.

action.description: The action's name, as the card's A2UI names it.

contextJson.description: The action's context, a JSON object in a string, when the card gives one.

MessageSent.description: The message is in the agent's queue. It appears in `/messages` once the agent starts on it, with `messageId` in its `sentIds`.

messageId.description: The message's id on the record.

TurnStop.description: A stop asked for. A stop ends the agent's turn as the page's Stop does; work it was doing stays on the board.

stopped.description: Whether a turn was running in it to stop.

Upload.description: A file put in the conversation's sandbox, to send with a message by `id` within 24 hours.

conversationId.description: The conversation it was uploaded to: only a message there sends it.

name.description: Its name in the sandbox, which may differ from the one given when a file of that name was there.

expiresAt.description: When `id` stops naming it; the file stays in the sandbox.

ConversationEvent.description: One event of a conversation's live stream: `kind` and its payload in the field of that name. A kind a client does not know is skipped.

kind.description: `text`: the agent's words as they come. `step`: a step starting or ending. `turn`: a turn starting or ending. `sent`: a person's message taken. `message`: a message kept.

StreamText.description: Words the agent is writing now; the message that keeps them follows as `message`.

phrase.description: What it is doing, in the request's language.

StreamMessage.description: A message: for `sent`, the `messageId` a send answered; for `message`, a `Message.id` to read with `after`.

DeviceEnded.description: A device signed out: its tokens stopped working, its open streams closed. Calling with them now answers `access-removed`.
